introduction: This foundational level introduces the concept of 'Negotiability', which essentially means the free transferability of commercial paper as a substitute for money. It breaks down the three specific instruments governed by the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.

core_concepts.title: What is a Negotiable Instrument? (Section 13)
core_concepts.description:
A 'negotiable instrument' means a promissory note, bill of exchange, or cheque payable either to order or to bearer.
- Core Characteristic: It is a document guaranteeing the payment of a specific amount of money, either on demand or at a set time, whose legal ownership can be transferred simply by delivery or by endorsement and delivery. It acts as a substitute for cash in commerce.

core_concepts.title: Promissory Note (Section 4)
core_concepts.description:
An instrument in writing (not being a bank-note or currency-note) containing an unconditional **undertaking**, signed by the maker, to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person, or to the bearer of the instrument.
- Parties: 2 (Maker - who promises to pay, and Payee - to whom the promise is made).
- Nature: It is a promise to pay (e.g., 'I promise to pay B or order Rs. 500').

core_concepts.title: Bill of Exchange (Section 5)
core_concepts.description:
An instrument in writing containing an unconditional **order**, signed by the maker, directing a certain person to pay a certain sum of money only to, or to the order of, a certain person or to the bearer.
- Parties: 3 (Drawer - who gives the order, Drawee - who is ordered to pay, and Payee - to whom payment is made).
- Nature: It is a command/order to pay (e.g., A orders B to pay C Rs. 500).

core_concepts.title: Cheque (Section 6)
core_concepts.description:
A cheque is a specialized Bill of Exchange drawn on a **specified banker** and not expressed to be payable otherwise than on demand.
- Distinctive Feature: While all cheques are bills of exchange, not all bills of exchange are cheques. A cheque MUST be drawn on a bank and is ALWAYS payable immediately on demand.
- Additions: It includes an electronic image of a truncated cheque and a cheque in electronic form.

important_entities.name: Unconditional Nature
important_entities.key_fact: NIs cannot depend on uncertain events.
important_entities.significance: A valid Promissory Note or Bill of Exchange MUST be unconditional. If A writes 'I promise to pay B Rs. 500 if B marries C' or 'I will pay when my ship arrives', it is NOT a valid negotiable instrument because the condition makes payment uncertain.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Can a citizen issue a Promissory Note payable to 'bearer' on demand? **NO**. Under Section 31 of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Act, ONLY the RBI or the Central Government can issue a promissory note payable to bearer on demand. This is to prevent private citizens from essentially printing their own currency notes.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A Promissory Note has 2 parties (Maker, Payee). Bills and Cheques have 3 (Drawer, Drawee, Payee).

exam_strategy_tips: If a Judiciary question asks 'Is a currency note a Promissory Note under the NIA?', the definitive answer is **NO**, as Section 4 explicitly excludes bank-notes and currency-notes from its ambit.
